newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: HOTEL LITHUANIA COULD GO FOR $10 MILLION.
newsitem.headline: HOTEL LITHUANIA COULD GO FOR $10 MILLION.

text.p: Lithuania could privatise the Hotel Lithuania for $10 million, despite the fact that an offer for the same amount was turned down by an earlier government, the chairman of the privatisation commission said on Thursday.
"The government said then that $10 million was too small, so that government rejected the proposal," Eduardas Vilkas told Reuters. "But It think we would now sell it for $10 million."
Vilkas said the ministry for municipal affairs was preparing the privatisation programme.
"We decided not to look for a separate adviser for the privatisation because this company is not very complex," Vilkas said. "They should complete the programme in May or June."
Hotel Lithuania is one of 13 state-owned companies slated for privatisation by open international tender in 1997 and 1998.
The 316-room Hotel Lithuania is 70 percent state-owned and has 344 employees.
